what_this_is: Every parameter the sweep passes to the geometry whose value does NOT vary across the
sweep. If a number reaches an OpenSCAD module as a named argument and is the same on
all 132 buildable variants, it is a setting, and it belongs here rather than in Python.
These are not axes. The axes live in variant_param/*.csv and are combined factorially,
so a column added there multiplies the variant count; the values below are the same on
every variant by design, and changing one moves the whole sweep together.
The membership test is mechanical, not a matter of taste: resolve the Parameters tree
for every variant in all three families, collect what each numeric field actually takes,
and keep the fields that come back with exactly one value. That is how boom_tolerance
and cowl_flange_tolerance were found -- neither sits near the others in the source, and
neither is named like a setting at its definition site.
What is deliberately NOT here: the coefficients inside derivation formulas -- the 4 in
max(panel_thickness, 4), the 3 in max(3*U, 3), the 2*U in the cowl flange height. Those
are scaling rules rather than parameters; the sweep never passes them to geometry as
values, it passes what they produce. Turning a rule into data is a different decision
and has not been made.
Read by fuselage_variants.load_constants(). Every key below is required and no other key
is accepted -- a typo is an error rather than a silently ignored row, and a value the
sweep needs can never go missing and be replaced by a default.
Changing a value re-renders on the next --resume: these reach the generated part
definitions by value, and that is what the staleness comparison reads.

tolerances._about: Clearances between mating parts. Every one is spacing that is MEANT to be there: it accommodates manufacturing variation and adhesive bond thickness, so a joint built with no gap has nowhere for the bond to go and nothing to absorb print variation. Refused if negative -- none of these joints is an interference fit.

longeron_tolerance.why: Clearance on the longeron tube in the corner's bore and in the chamfer that leads into it.

greeble_tolerance.why: The snap-fit clearance between the bulkhead's greeble post and the corner's socket. Carried entirely on the CORNER -- its bore is opened out by this much and the bulkhead's post stays nominal, so the joint takes the clearance once. There is deliberately no bulkhead counterpart; 'the post is nominal' is an invariant, not a setting.

corner_tolerance.why: Clearance on the two corner faces that seat against the bulkhead -- the flat at flat_x and the diagonal -- over the corner's full height. Carried entirely on the corner, same as the greeble: when the bulkhead re-evaluates that shape to cut its own socket it passes 0. Held at 0 because 0 is what every flown part was built at. OPEN: if these faces are bonded, 0 leaves no bond line.

panel_tolerance.why: The gap the panel stands off the flange face by, so its outer surface still lands flush with the mold line at corner_radius. Applies only where there IS a panel: a cowling bulkhead and the 0 mm panel variants take 0, and that zero is structural rather than a setting -- no panel, no gap to leave.

boom_tolerance.why: Clearance on the boom tube in the boom bulkhead's collet: collet_radius = boom_diameter/2 + boom_collet_thickness + boom_tolerance. Four times the longeron's 0.05 and nothing on record says why -- the boom is a larger tube through a deeper bore, but the number has never been justified in writing.

cowl_flange_tolerance.why: Clearance between the bulkhead's cowl-mounting flange and the cowl that slides over it. Sets the flange's outer radius at corner_radius - extrusion_width - cowl_flange_tolerance. Applies only to a cowling bulkhead; every other type takes 0, and that zero is structural -- there is no cowl flange on a bulkhead that mounts no cowl.

geometry._about: Shape of the part rather than fit between parts. Constant across the sweep for the same reason the tolerances are -- nothing derives them from size -- but they are not clearances and are not subject to the non-negative rule.

greeble_opening_angle.why: Half-angle of the wedge cut out of the greeble, so the mouth is 70 degrees wide. That mouth is what makes the greeble a C rather than a closed ring, and it is how the longeron is assembled: the tube presses in sideways and snaps into the bore, which the chord across the mouth (2*r*sin35 = 57% of the tube diameter) is narrow enough to hold. Arrived at by experiment -- a tuned value, not a derived one. Do not replace it with a formula.

boom_key_angle.why: Rotation of the anti-rotation key around the boom tube, in degrees. The upper and lower webs mirror it as 180 - boom_key_angle, so 0 puts the key on the fuselage centerline. Never anything but 0 in the sweep; it exists because the key does not have to be there.

printer._about: Properties of the machine, not of the design. The same airframe printed on a different nozzle wants different numbers here and no other change. Refused if not strictly positive.

extrusion_width.why: Nozzle width the sweep sizes printed features against -- the greeble wall, the bulkhead flange and the cowl flange are all whole multiples of it. Was written out seven separate times across three files, each overriding a PrinterSettings default of 0.4 that nothing wanted; the default now comes from here and the overrides are gone. The hand drivers in scad/ are still at 0.4 and that is deliberate, not drift.

layer_height.why: Layer height the sweep sizes printed features against. Only plate_thickness = ceil(4*U) * layer_height reads it today. Unlike extrusion_width this was never overridden anywhere -- it sat as a dataclass default -- so the two halves of one machine profile were configured in opposite ways.
